testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure cargo is loaded properly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver has four main responsibilities with cargo. They must inspect the cargo, check for overloads and unbalanced weight, make sure the cargo is secured and does not block their view, and ensure the cargo does not block access to emergency equipment.

questions.question: On long trips, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue on long trips, take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving. Driving through the night or during times when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Bridges usually:
questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Expect other vehicles to move out of your way.
Wait until you are in an intersection to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes slowly and smoothly.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This keeps your vehicle under control and gives other drivers time to see your movement and react.

questions.question: Why should you regularly drain the air tanks?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
To allow for a change in pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the air tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these materials. With a manual drain valve, drain the tank at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you will still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, the safest speed is:

options.text: The same speed as surrounding traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles travel in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: If brakes fail on a long downhill grade, the driver should:

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and back on to reset the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill grade, use an escape ramp. If no escape ramp is available, look for another way to stop, such as a side road or open field.

questions.question: While driving a CMV:

options.text: You may hold a cell phone to receive a call.
You may not hold a cell phone to make a call.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hold a cell phone to make a call.
questions.explanation: While driving a CMV, you cannot make voice calls while holding your phone or pressing more than one button. You also cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: When completing an offset back/right parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must be parked completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Puts the cargo in a large box
Stops cargo from sliding during transport
Stops others from buying the cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from moving while the vehicle is in transit.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you will slow down, you should:

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal.
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
Swerve side to side to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights.
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells drivers behind you that you are slowing down. It is important to communicate with other drivers.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You should not use your mirrors.
You should not use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should use your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors before changing lanes.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: How much you drink
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends mainly on how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: If air pressure drops to between ____, a visual low pressure warning signal should already be on.
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 and 75 psi
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal should turn on before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Alcohol is removed from the body:

options.text: More quickly if you stay awake

questions.correctAnswerText: At a fixed rate
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Drinking coffee or taking a cold shower will not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.question: Blocking is used to:

options.text: Put cargo in a large box
Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer
Stop cargo from falling out of a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop cargo from sliding in a trailer
questions.explanation: Blocking is used on all sides of cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: A pre-trip inspection should include:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the engine oil level
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check the engine oil level, radiator coolant level, and condition of the hoses.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, decide what to do quickly because:

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail on a downhill slope, act quickly. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Pressed down slowly
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly for a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number of vehicles passed
questions.explanation: An Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) must show the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must include trip dates and total distance traveled. It does not need to include how many vehicles were passed.

questions.question: Hanging meat in a refrigerated truck:

options.text: Is a good way for inexperienced drivers to gain experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires a skilled driver.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is an unstable load. It has a high center of gravity and swings during transport. This affects how the driver can control the vehicle. Only a skilled driver should transport this type of cargo.

questions.question: Once cargo is secured onto a vehicle:

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
You should not let others inspect the cargo.
You should check the cargo every 150 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should check the cargo every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security before starting your trip, within the first 50 miles, and then every 150 miles or every three hours after that.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle when exiting and keep three points of contact with it at all times. For buses, hold the handrail. If you exit incorrectly during the skills test, you may fail.

questions.question: ____ is required emergency equipment.
questions.correctAnswerText: A spare electrical fuse
questions.explanation: All commercial vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Hydroplaning:

options.text: Usually happens when vehicles are traveling faster than 65 mph.
Can occur with a minimal amount of water on the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can occur with a minimal amount of water on the roadway.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip with the road and slide on water. You do not need a large amount of water on the road for this to happen.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brakes before slowing down. Your brake lights will flash to warn drivers behind you.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Are used to move air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and oil that can damage the brake system. Air tanks have drain valves to remove this water and oil.

questions.question: Loading cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
Increases the likelihood that items will fall down.
Increases the difficulty of unloading the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity increases the risk that a vehicle will tip over. Load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: When encountering a railroad crossing during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if the other vehicle is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while on railroad tracks.

questions.question: What is the name of a thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road through it. It looks like a wet road. Be very careful when it is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light might be:

options.text: Someone who does not know traffic rules

questions.correctAnswerText: An impaired driver
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, use drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. Stopping at green lights is one sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections should be done:

options.text: Differently each time to check different items
The same way each time so you don't forget anything

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This routine helps you learn all the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: If brakes overheat going down a hill, they may:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop working
questions.explanation: Using brakes too much can cause them to overheat and stop working well. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: Look ahead at the road ____ in front of your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 seconds
questions.explanation: Good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and react. Watch for vehicles entering the highway or changing into your lane.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots on the road where tar is bleeding:

options.text: Have the same grip as the rest of the road
Have more grip than the rest of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very slippery
questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar in the road rises to the surface. These spots are very slippery. Be careful when you see them.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Let poisonous fumes into the cab

questions.correctAnswerText: Let poisonous fumes into the cab
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air
Start pumping air into the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air
questions.explanation: The governor stops the compressor when air pressure reaches about 125 psi. This level is called the cut-out level.

questions.question: What happens if the exhaust system is not working properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab
Fumes may come out the back of the muffler

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab
questions.explanation: Leaks in the exhaust system are very dangerous. Toxic fumes can enter the cab or sleeper area and hurt drivers and passengers.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators are:

options.text: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems
Only allowed in northern parts of the state

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol to air brake systems
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. These devices add alcohol to the brake system to prevent ice from forming.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a distracted driver?
questions.correctAnswerText: Give them plenty of space.
questions.explanation: When you see a distracted driver, keep a safe distance from them and stay away.

questions.question: How much should you reduce your speed on a wet road?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one-third.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, reduce your speed by about one-third because traction is reduced.

questions.question: Can you have more than one driver's license?

options.text: Yes, if one is for business purposes.
Yes, if they are issued by different states.
No, you can only have one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, you can only have one license.
questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver's license at a time. States share information to prevent this. Breaking this law can result in fines or jail time.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing and call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: When planning to change lanes, how often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: You don't need to check them.
Check them more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors regularly, but check them even more often when changing lanes.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when used, what does this mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: They need to be checked.
questions.explanation: Brakes pulling to one side is a sign of brake trouble. Have them checked right away.

questions.question: Why should you check your tires often in very hot weather?

options.text: Tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases with heat.
questions.explanation: Hot weather causes tire air pressure to increase. Check your tire pressure and mounting regularly when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
Tires cannot drive well in wet weather.
Water has not yet absorbed dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, water mixes with oil and grease on the road surface. This creates a slippery film that has not yet washed away.

questions.question: When making a left turn, when should you start the turn?

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection.
At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
After your rear wheels have passed the center.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or after reaching the center of the intersection.
questions.explanation: Start your left turn at the center of the intersection or after. Turning too early can cause the left side of your vehicle to hit another vehicle.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Should only be done in poor weather.
Stops cargo from sliding during transport.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport.
questions.explanation: Blocking is used to keep cargo from sliding while the vehicle is moving.
